title: The Lady, or the Tiger?
subtitle: 美女還是老虎？史托克頓沒有寫完的結局
source: 原創導讀；故事原文依 Project Gutenberg《The Lady, or the Tiger?》（1882，公版），背景依 Wikipedia〈The Lady, or the Tiger?〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Frank R. Stockton, The Lady, or the Tiger? (1882), Project Gutenberg
Wikipedia: The Lady, or the Tiger?

beginner.title: Two Doors
paras: Long ago, a king had a strange way of judging people. When a man was accused of a crime, he was taken into a big arena. In front of him were two doors. Behind one door was a hungry tiger. Behind the other was a beautiful lady.
很久以前，有一位國王用一種奇怪的方式審判人。當一個男人被指控犯罪時，他會被帶進一個巨大的競技場。他面前有兩扇門：一扇門後是一隻飢餓的老虎，另一扇門後是一位美麗的女子。

The man had to open one door. If the tiger came out, it ate him, and everyone said he was guilty. If the lady came out, he was innocent, and he had to marry her right away. Nobody could hear anything through the thick doors. It was all chance. The crowd watched every trial.
這個男人必須打開其中一扇門。如果出來的是老虎，牠會吃掉他，大家就說他有罪。如果出來的是女子，他就是無罪的，而且必須立刻娶她。厚厚的門讓人聽不到任何聲音。一切全憑運氣。群眾會觀看每一場審判。

The king’s daughter, the princess, loved a young man who was not rich or royal. When the king found out, he sent the young man to the arena. His only “crime” was loving someone so far above him. But the princess learned the secret: she knew which door hid the tiger and which hid the lady.
國王的女兒——公主——愛上了一個既不富有也不是王族的年輕人。國王發現後，把年輕人送進了競技場。他唯一的「罪」，就是愛上了一個身分比他高太多的人。但公主打聽到了祕密：她知道哪扇門後是老虎，哪扇門後是女子。

There was a problem. The lady behind the door was a girl the princess hated, because she thought the girl also liked the young man. In the arena, the young man looked at the princess. She quietly moved her hand to the right. He opened the door on the right.
問題來了。門後的女子，是公主討厭的一個女孩，因為公主認為那女孩也喜歡這個年輕人。在競技場上，年輕人望向公主。她悄悄地把手往右一指。他打開了右邊那扇門。

What came out? The writer, Frank Stockton, never tells us. The story was published in 1882 and ends with a question: “Which came out of the opened door — the lady, or the tiger?” Readers have argued about the answer ever since. What do you think?
出來的是什麼？作者法蘭克．史托克頓始終沒有告訴我們。這個故事在 1882 年發表，以一個問題作結：「從打開的門裡出來的，是美女，還是老虎？」從此讀者們就一直爭論答案。你覺得呢？

intermediate.title: The Lady, or the Tiger?
paras: Frank R. Stockton’s short story “The Lady, or the Tiger?”, first published in The Century Magazine in November 1882, is famous for one reason: it refuses to end. Set in an imaginary kingdom ruled by a “semi-barbaric king”, it builds towards a single moment of decision and then hands that decision to the reader.
法蘭克．R．史托克頓的短篇小說〈美女還是老虎？〉，1882 年 11 月首次刊登於《世紀雜誌》，它之所以出名，只有一個原因：它拒絕結束。故事發生在一個由「半野蠻國王」統治的虛構王國，情節一路推向一個決定的瞬間，然後把這個決定交給讀者。

The king has invented a public system of justice that depends entirely on chance. An accused man enters an arena and must open one of two identical doors. The doors are so thick that no sound can pass through them. Behind one waits a hungry tiger, which kills him if he chooses it, proving his guilt. Behind the other waits a lady, whom he must marry at once, proving his innocence. Stockton calls the arena “an agent of poetic justice”, but his tone is clearly ironic.
國王發明了一套完全依賴運氣的公開審判制度。被告走進競技場，必須打開兩扇一模一樣的門之一。那兩扇門厚到任何聲音都傳不出來。一扇門後等著一隻飢餓的老虎，選了牠就會被咬死，證明他有罪；另一扇門後等著一位女子，他必須立刻娶她，證明他無罪。史托克頓稱這座競技場是「詩意正義的代理人」，但他的語氣顯然帶著反諷。

Trouble begins when the king discovers that his daughter loves a young courtier of low rank. The young man is put on trial in the arena. His only crime, in the king’s eyes, is daring to love someone so far above him in rank. The princess, using her power and gold, learns which door hides the tiger and which hides the lady. Worse, she knows the lady chosen for him — a beautiful young woman she suspects of loving him too, and whom she hates.
麻煩始於國王發現女兒愛上了一個地位低微的年輕朝臣。年輕人被送上競技場受審。在國王眼中，他唯一的罪就是膽敢愛上身分遠高於他的人。公主利用權勢和金錢，打聽出哪扇門後是老虎、哪扇門後是女子。更糟的是，她認識那位被選給他的女子——一個美麗的年輕女子，公主懷疑她也愛著這個年輕人，並且恨她。

When the young man enters, he looks at the princess and understands that she knows the secret. Without hesitation, she moves her hand slightly to the right, and he opens the right-hand door. At this moment, Stockton stops telling the story. Instead, he describes the princess’s agony: she will lose her lover either way — to death or to another woman.
年輕人走進場時，望向公主，明白她知道祕密。她毫不遲疑地把手微微往右一指，他便打開了右邊的門。就在這一刻，史托克頓停止講故事，轉而描寫公主的痛苦：不管怎樣，她都會失去愛人——不是失去給死亡，就是失去給另一個女人。

The story ends with a direct challenge: “And so I leave it with all of you: Which came out of the opened door — the lady, or the tiger?” Stockton later wrote a sequel, but it does not answer the question either. The open ending forces readers to think about human nature, jealousy and love, and to defend their answer with evidence from the text.
故事以一個直接的挑戰作結：「那麼，我把這個問題留給你們每一位：從打開的門裡出來的，是美女，還是老虎？」史托克頓後來寫了一篇續集，但也沒有回答這個問題。開放式的結局，迫使讀者思考人性、嫉妒與愛，並用文本中的證據為自己的答案辯護。

advanced.title: An Ending Left to the Reader
paras: Few short stories have generated as much argument from so little resolution as Frank R. Stockton’s “The Lady, or the Tiger?”, published in The Century Magazine in November 1882. The story’s fame rests on a deliberate refusal. Having constructed a situation of maximum suspense, Stockton withholds the outcome and transfers the burden of judgement to the reader. The result is less a conventional tale than a carefully engineered thought experiment about human motivation.
很少有短篇小說像法蘭克．R．史托克頓的〈美女還是老虎？〉一樣，以如此少的結局引發如此多的爭論。這篇小說在 1882 年 11 月刊登於《世紀雜誌》，它的名氣建立在一個刻意的拒絕上：史托克頓建構了一個懸念達到頂點的情境，卻扣住結果，把判斷的重擔轉交給讀者。結果，它與其說是一個傳統的故事，不如說是一場精心設計、關於人類動機的思想實驗。

The setting is an imaginary kingdom ruled by a “semi-barbaric king”, whose ideas, the narrator notes, have been “polished and sharpened” by civilised neighbours yet remain essentially extravagant. His system of justice reflects this mixture. An accused man must choose between two identical doors in a public arena: behind one is a hungry tiger, behind the other a lady whom he must marry immediately. Stockton describes the arena, with conspicuous irony, as “an agent of poetic justice, in which crime was punished, or virtue rewarded, by the decrees of an impartial and incorruptible chance.”
故事背景是一個由「半野蠻國王」統治的虛構王國。敘事者指出，這位國王的想法雖然被文明的鄰國「打磨得更加精煉」，本質上卻依然鋪張奢華。他的審判制度正反映了這種混合：被告必須在公開競技場中，在兩扇一模一樣的門之間做選擇——一扇門後是飢餓的老虎，另一扇門後是一位他必須立刻迎娶的女子。史托克頓以明顯的反諷，把這座競技場形容為「詩意正義的代理人，罪行受罰或美德獲賞，全由公正而清廉的機運來裁決」。

The moral dilemma falls not on the accused but on the princess. Her lover, a handsome youth of low rank, has been condemned to the arena. She alone has discovered which door conceals which fate, and she recognises the waiting lady as a rival she hates. Gold, and the power of her will, had brought her the secret. When the young man looks to her, she moves her hand to the right without hesitation, and he opens that door. Stockton then pivots from narrative to analysis, asking the reader to consider the princess, “that hot-blooded, semi-barbaric princess, her soul at a white heat beneath the combined fires of despair and jealousy.”

道德兩難並不落在被告身上，而是落在公主身上。她的愛人——一位英俊卻地位低微的青年——被判進入競技場。只有她查出了哪扇門後藏著哪種命運，而她認出那位等待的女子是她痛恨的情敵。黃金，加上她的意志力，讓她得到了這個祕密。當年輕人望向她時，她毫不遲疑地把手往右一指，他便打開了那扇門。接著，史托克頓從敘事轉向分析，要讀者想想這位公主——「那位熱血的、半野蠻的公主，她的靈魂在絕望與嫉妒交織的烈火下燒得白熱」。

The narrator’s commentary is carefully balanced. He imagines her horror at the thought of her lover torn by the tiger, and equally her anguish at picturing him joyfully reunited with her rival. Her decision, he says, was indicated in an instant but made after “days and nights of anguished deliberation.” Every argument for one door is matched by an argument for the other, so that the text supports both readings. Stockton later published a sequel in 1885, “The Discourager of Hesitancy”, but it too declined to reveal the answer.
敘事者的評論拿捏得十分平衡。他想像公主一想到愛人被老虎撕裂時的恐懼，也同樣想像她看見他與情敵歡喜團聚時的痛苦。他說，她的決定雖然在一瞬間就指示出來，卻是經過「無數個日夜的痛苦思量」才做出的。每一個支持某扇門的論點，都有一個支持另一扇門的論點與之對應，使得文本同時支持兩種解讀。史托克頓後來在 1885 年發表續集〈猶豫勸阻官〉，但它同樣拒絕揭曉答案。

The story ends by addressing its audience directly: “And so I leave it with all of you: Which came out of the opened door,—the lady, or the tiger?” That final sentence turns readers into judges, much as the king’s arena turned chance into a judge. For students, the story offers an ideal exercise in argument. There is no correct answer to look up; there is only the evidence of the text — the princess’s jealousy, her love, her “semi-barbaric” nature — and the quality of the reasoning built upon it.
故事最後直接對讀者說話：「那麼，我把這個問題留給你們每一位：從打開的門裡出來的，是美女，還是老虎？」最後這句話把讀者變成了法官，就像國王的競技場把機運變成了法官一樣。對學生來說，這個故事是練習論證的理想素材：沒有標準答案可查，只有文本中的證據——公主的嫉妒、她的愛、她「半野蠻」的天性——以及建立在這些證據之上的推理品質。

quote.text: And so I leave it with all of you: Which came out of the opened door,—the lady, or the tiger?
quote.author: Frank R. Stockton

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to open heavy doors safely.
How kings trained tigers in an arena.
Why the princess married a rich man.
A story that ends with a question for readers.
beginner.evidence: The story was published in 1882 and ends with a question
beginner.why: 全文：一則沒有給出結局的故事。
traps: 字面誤讀：門只是情節的一部分。
捏造：文中沒提訓練老虎。
正反顛倒：她愛的是不富有的年輕人。

beginner.q: What does “the secret” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Why the young man had fallen in love with her.
Which door hid the tiger and which hid the lady.
How the king usually judged people who did wrong.
Who had built the big arena for the king.
beginner.evidence: she knew which door hid the tiger and which hid the lady
beginner.why: 同一句冒號後面直接說明。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：他們相愛是大家已知的事，不是秘密。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：判決方式是公開的。
捏造：文中沒提競技場是誰蓋的。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Frank Stockton told readers the ending.
The princess pointed to the left door.
The young man opened the door on the right.
People could hear sounds through the doors.
beginner.evidence: He opened the door on the right.
traps: 正反顛倒：作者沒有告訴我們。
正反顛倒：她指向右邊。
正反顛倒：門很厚，聽不到。

beginner.q: Why is the princess’s choice so hard?
options: She will lose the young man either way.
She does not know where the tiger is.
She wants the young man to marry the lady.
She is afraid the crowd will hear her.
beginner.evidence: The lady behind the door was a girl the princess hated
beginner.why: 不管選哪扇門，她都會失去他：被老虎吃掉或娶別人。
traps: 正反顛倒：她知道秘密。
正反顛倒：她恨那位女子。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：門很厚，是門後的聲音傳不出來。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: The story makes readers decide its ending themselves.
The king’s justice was fair to every person.
The princess wanted the tiger to win.
Stockton’s sequel finally gave the answer.
intermediate.evidence: it builds towards a single moment of decision and then hands that decision to the reader
traps: 正反顛倒：作者語帶諷刺。
過度推論：故事沒有說她怎麼選。
正反顛倒：續集也沒有答案。

intermediate.q: What does the author mean by saying Stockton’s tone is “ironic”?
options: He makes the story sound sad and slow.
He praises the king as a true hero.
He calls the arena fair while showing it depends on chance.
He writes the story as a real history.
intermediate.evidence: Stockton calls the arena “an agent of poetic justice”, but his tone is clearly ironic.
intermediate.why: 他嘴上說公正，實際上完全靠運氣，這就是反諷。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：讓人苦惱的是公主的兩難，不是語氣慢。
正反顛倒：作者在嘲諷國王。
正反顛倒：這是想像的王國，不是真實歷史。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The young man was a prince from another country.
The princess used her power and gold to learn the secret.
The lady was someone the princess loved.
The story first appeared in a book in 1885.
intermediate.evidence: The princess, using her power and gold, learns which door hides the tiger
traps: 正反顛倒：他身分低微。
正反顛倒：她恨那位女子。
時序錯置：1882 年刊在雜誌，1885 年是續集。

intermediate.q: Why does Stockton describe the princess’s agony instead of the ending?
options: To show how much the king loved his daughter.
To hide the fact that the tiger had already escaped.
To prove that the young man was guilty of a crime.
To make readers weigh her love against her jealousy.
intermediate.evidence: she will lose her lover either way — to death or to another woman
intermediate.why: 第四段：把焦點放在她的兩難，讓讀者自己判斷。
traps: 正反顛倒：國王反而懲罰她的愛人。
捏造：老虎一直在門後。
正反顛倒：他唯一的罪是愛上公主。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that the tiger came out of the door.
To show how the story turns readers into judges.
To describe the history of real arenas in Rome.
To argue that the king’s justice was truly fair.
advanced.evidence: That final sentence turns readers into judges
traps: 正反顛倒：作者說兩種解讀都成立。
捏造：這是想像的王國。
正反顛倒：作者說這種公正帶有明顯反諷。

advanced.q: What does “impartial and incorruptible chance” suggest about the king’s justice, as Stockton presents it?
options: It depends on how the crowd decides to vote.
It is controlled carefully by wise judges.
It always punishes the people who are guilty.
It is called fair, but it really depends on luck.
advanced.evidence: Stockton describes the arena, with conspicuous irony, as “an agent of poetic justice
advanced.why: 作者以明顯的反諷稱讚它公正，其實只是運氣。
traps: 捏造：群眾只是觀看。
正反顛倒：沒有法官判斷。
正反顛倒：結果全靠運氣。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Stockton’s 1885 sequel also refused to reveal the answer.
The princess hesitated a long time in the arena.
The young man was of royal birth.
The narrator says the princess chose the lady.
advanced.evidence: it too declined to reveal the answer
traps: 正反顛倒：她毫不猶豫地示意。
正反顛倒：他身分低微。
正反顛倒：作者沒有說。

advanced.q: What can be inferred about the narrator’s commentary on the princess?
options: It shows the princess did not love the man.
It clearly favours the tiger as the answer.
It is balanced so that both doors can be argued for.
It reveals that the princess opened the door herself.
advanced.evidence: Every argument for one door is matched by an argument for the other
traps: 正反顛倒：敘述者說她對兩種結果都痛苦。
以偏概全：兩邊的論點都有。
張冠李戴：開門的是年輕人。

reflections: Which came out of the door — the lady or the tiger? Write a paragraph defending your answer with at least two pieces of evidence from the story.
Is an open ending satisfying or frustrating? Give an example of another book, film or series with an ending you had to decide for yourself.

Using gold and the power of her will, she alone has discovered which door hides which fate, and she recognises the waiting lady as a rival she hates. When the young man looks to her, she moves her hand to the right without hesitation, and he opens that door.
道德的兩難不落在被告身上，而是落在公主身上。她的愛人——一位英俊卻地位低微的青年——被送進了競技場。靠著金錢和自己的意志力，只有她查出了哪扇門後藏著哪種命運，而她認出那位等待的女子是她痛恨的情敵。當年輕人望向她時，她毫不遲疑地把手往右一指，他便打開了那扇門。

At this point, Stockton turns from storytelling to analysis. He asks the reader to imagine the princess’s horror at the thought of her lover torn by the tiger, and equally her pain at picturing him happily married to her rival. Her decision, he says, was shown in an instant but made after “days and nights of anguished deliberation.” Every argument for one door is matched by an argument for the other. Yet not even a sequel published in 1885 revealed the answer.
說到這裡，史托克頓從敘事轉向分析。他要讀者想像，公主想到愛人被老虎撕裂時的恐懼，以及想到他和情敵幸福成婚時同樣的痛苦。他說，她的決定雖然在一瞬間顯示出來，卻是經過「日日夜夜痛苦的考慮」才做出的。支持某一扇門的每個理由，都有支持另一扇門的理由相抗衡。然而連 1885 年出版的續集，也沒有揭曉答案。

The story ends by addressing its readers directly: “And so I leave it with all of you: Which came out of the opened door,—the lady, or the tiger?” That final sentence turns readers into judges, much as the king’s arena turned chance into a judge. It is evidence from the text that students must rely on, not a correct answer to look up. Only by weighing that evidence can a reader defend an answer. The princess’s jealousy, her love and her “semi-barbaric” nature are all the clues there are.
故事最後直接對讀者說：「所以我把它交給你們每一個人：從打開的門裡出來的，是美女，還是老虎？」這最後一句把讀者變成了法官，就像國王的競技場把機運變成了法官。學生能依靠的，是文本裡的證據，而不是一個可以查到的標準答案。只有權衡這些證據，讀者才能為自己的答案辯護。公主的嫉妒、她的愛和她「半野蠻」的天性，就是全部的線索。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a story with no ending turns readers into judges.
How kings trained tigers for public arenas.
Why the princess married a rich young man.
How Stockton wrote a sequel that solved the mystery.
questions.evidence: That final sentence turns readers into judges
questions.why: 全文：故事刻意不給結局，把判斷交給讀者。
traps: 捏造：文中沒提訓練老虎。
正反顛倒：她愛的是地位低微的青年。
正反顛倒：續集也沒有揭曉答案。

questions.q: What does Stockton’s description of the arena as “an agent of poetic justice” suggest?
options: He thinks the arena was built by poets.
He believes it is the best system of justice.
He praises it as fair while showing it depends on luck.
He wants readers to admire the king’s wisdom.
questions.evidence: With conspicuous irony, Stockton calls the arena “an agent of poetic justice”
questions.why: 作者以明顯的反諷稱它公正，其實全靠機運。
traps: 字面誤讀：poetic justice 不是詩人蓋的。
正反顛倒：他是在反諷。
正反顛倒：作者稱國王「半野蠻」。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The young man was a prince from a rich kingdom.
The princess moved her hand to the right without hesitation.
Sounds could be heard clearly through the doors.
The story first appeared in The Century Magazine in 1885.
questions.evidence: she moves her hand to the right without hesitation
traps: 正反顛倒：他地位低微。
正反顛倒：門厚到聽不到聲音。
數字錯位：1882 年，1885 年是續集。

questions.q: Here is a sentence: “Readers have argued about the answer ever since.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?
options: Paragraph 2.
Paragraph 3.
Paragraph 4.
Paragraph 5.
questions.evidence: Yet not even a sequel published in 1885 revealed the answer.
questions.why: 第四段結尾說連續集都沒揭曉答案，接「讀者從此爭論不休」最順；ever since 也呼應前一句的時間點。
traps: 位置陷阱：第二段在介紹審判制度，還沒有懸念。
位置陷阱：第三段結尾才剛打開門，還沒到「沒答案」。
位置陷阱：第五段已是收尾，談的是讀者成為法官。
